ideas.title: Popcorn meadow you can climb
ideas.critique: Real GPU spheres that collide, stack and pile into a climbable hill, plus a stand-longest dare, are physics the island has never had, and you can play it again. Burying the friends and the hill growing echo the dunes, and the sunset eat-back is a scripted reset. It all depends on the launches and the pile looking solid on film.

ideas.title: The ground is a drum skin
ideas.critique: A real wave equation on the terrain, with rings that interfere into a launching spike, is a new way the ground moves, and the player can drive it with one key. The terrain has been reshaped island-wide before, though. If the rings are low and the riders just slide on the heightfield, it reads as a wobbly floor, not a drum.

ideas.title: Lumi shrinks to 2 cm
ideas.critique: House-sized dew drops bending the sun at grass height is a strong showcase for Hikari, and the change of scale is one the player has never felt. Under it, it is one more Lumi body trick shot close, the friends calling Lumi's name is a scripted search, and the island's coarse grass and props may fall apart at beetle scale.

ideas.title: The island is a pinball table
ideas.critique: A chrome ball that reflects the whole island while it rolls with real physics, played on two keys, is a playable showcase of the tracer. Tilting the island toward a shore is the seesaw again, and turning the island into a game table is close to the capped replace-the-island kind. The flipper trees and bumper friends will feel canned unless the ball's hits have weight.

ideas.title: A giant's picnic lands on the island
ideas.critique: Giant generated props with porcelain, steel and tea materials are a new place, and props and places are capped however new the premise. Swimming, licking and climbing will be scripted friend animations, so you watch it once as a walk-through.

ideas.title: A whale swims through the ground: it breaches
ideas.critique: The breach is the payoff round 1 was missing: a body tearing out of the turf on a ballistic arc, with soil particles and tossed props. It is still a scripted island-wide event filmed once, a generated asset's leap is easy to make stiff, and whether it lands depends on the soil splash being real particles that move the friends.
